implementation_notes: Default realization: one concurrency token on the root (SQL Server rowversion via [Timestamp]/IsRowVersion, or IsConcurrencyToken on a GUID/int you bump yourself) and none on the members. EF Core adds the token to the WHERE clause of every UPDATE and DELETE of the root, so a change made anywhere in the cluster since load surfaces as DbUpdateConcurrencyException at SaveChanges. It replaces per-member version columns and per-member locks with one token; choose it when conflicts are rare and the session is short.

variants.name: EF Core concurrency token on the aggregate root
variants.implementation_notes: Default realization: one concurrency token on the root (SQL Server rowversion via [Timestamp]/IsRowVersion, or IsConcurrencyToken on a GUID/int you bump yourself) and none on the members. EF Core adds the token to the WHERE clause of every UPDATE and DELETE of the root, so a change made anywhere in the cluster since load surfaces as DbUpdateConcurrencyException at SaveChanges. It replaces per-member version columns and per-member locks with one token; choose it when conflicts are rare and the session is short.
variants.idiom_name: EF Core concurrency token (rowversion / IsConcurrencyToken) on the root entity
pitfalls: The exception only fires when SaveChanges writes the root; a member update that does not touch the root row escapes the check - map members so that a cluster change always marks the root modified.
Retry loops must reload the root; reusing the same tracked entities after a conflict re-sends the same stale token.

variants.name: pessimistic root lock via raw SQL (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK)
variants.implementation_notes: EF Core has no pessimistic lock API, so the pessimistic realization is a raw-SQL query for the root with SQL Server's WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) - or its equivalent on other providers - inside an explicit transaction; the update lock is held until the transaction ends, so other writers of that root block. It replaces per-member locking with one root lock and is the choice when a conflict would be expensive or an edit session must not be re-done.
variants.idiom_name: FromSqlRaw("... WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) ...") in an explicit transaction
pitfalls: FromSql must return the full entity shape or EF Core cannot track it; add the include/join for members in a follow-up query while the transaction is still open.
UPDLOCK without ROWLOCK may escalate to page or table locks under load, blocking unrelated clusters - check the actual lock mode when clusters are hot.
